title: Student lacks legal basis for data sharing
description: Student may share assignment data without proper legal basis or consent from institution
assumptions: Assumes student is aware of data sharing requirements

title: Student provides excessive personal data
description: Student may include more personal information than necessary for assignment submission
assumptions: Assumes student may include unnecessary metadata

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Assignment data in transit could be intercepted by unauthorized parties
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted over network

title: Metadata linking parties
description: Transmission metadata (timestamps, IP addresses) could be used to link student to specific courses
assumptions: Assumes metadata is captured during transmission

title: Unauthorized access to grades portal
description: Grades portal may be accessed by unauthorized personnel or external parties
assumptions: Assumes portal has authentication controls

title: Excessive data retention
description: Portal may retain more student data than necessary for course administration
assumptions: Assumes data retention policies exist

title: Failure to notify about data processing
description: Students may not be notified about how their assignment data is processed and stored
assumptions: Assumes notification mechanisms exist

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Student data (student ID, course, file reference, requesting role) transmitted over the network could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, leading to unauthorized access to sensitive academic information.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network infrastructure that may not be fully secured

title: Unintended data access during transmission
description: Data in transit could be accessed by unintended parties (e.g., network attackers, compromised systems) who are not authorized to view student information.
assumptions: Network security controls may not be sufficient to prevent all unauthorized access

title: Potential lack of lawful basis for data sharing
description: The Grades Portal Web App may be sharing student data to the Assignment & Grading Service without a clear lawful basis or proper consent from students.
assumptions: Data sharing practices may not be fully documented or compliant with privacy regulations

title: Student identification through data sharing
description: Student ID is being shared with the Assignment & Grading Service, which could enable identification of individual students and their academic activities.
assumptions: Student IDs are unique identifiers that can be used to link data to specific individuals

title: Unauthorized access to stored student data
description: The Assignment & Grading Service may store student data in a way that allows unauthorized access, leading to potential disclosure of sensitive academic information.
assumptions: Access controls at the destination may not be sufficient to prevent unauthorized access

title: Student identification at destination
description: Student IDs, course information, and file references stored at the Assignment & Grading Service could be used to identify and profile individual students.
assumptions: Student IDs are unique identifiers that can be used to link data to specific individuals

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Student Assignment Data
description: The Assignment & Grading Service may share student assignment data (including student ID, course, and submission time) with unauthorized parties or in an insecure manner, leading to potential privacy breaches.

title: Potential Lawfulness Issues in Data Sharing
description: The sharing of student assignment data may not be fully lawful or compliant with applicable privacy regulations, particularly regarding consent and purpose limitation.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Assignment Data
description: The Assignment Store may be accessed by unauthorized individuals or systems, leading to potential disclosure of sensitive student information including submission details.

title: Inadequate Data Retention and Deletion
description: The Assignment Store may retain student assignment data beyond necessary retention periods, failing to properly delete data when no longer needed for legitimate purposes.

title: Data in Transit Privacy Risks
description: Assignment data transmitted from the Grading Service to the Assignment Store may contain metadata or be intercepted during transit, potentially revealing information about students and their submission patterns.

title: Lack of confidentiality of teacher credentials
description: Teacher's login credentials and authentication information may be exposed during the sharing process, potentially allowing unauthorized access to the system.
assumptions: Assumes teacher credentials are shared during login process

title: Lack of confidentiality in data transmission
description: Authentication tokens, credentials, and request data transmitted from teacher to grades portal may be intercepted by third parties during transit.
assumptions: Assumes data flows over network without guaranteed encryption

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student submissions
description: Grades portal may disclose student submission data to unauthorized parties or inappropriately share data with third parties upon receiving the teacher's request.
assumptions: Assumes portal has appropriate access controls and data handling procedures

title: Lawful basis for sharing student work with teacher
description: The portal may share student submissions without a clear lawful basis or proper authorization from students/parents, potentially violating data protection requirements.
assumptions: Assumes the portal operates without explicit consent mechanisms for data sharing with teachers.

title: Excessive information disclosure to teacher
description: The portal may disclose more student information than necessary for the teacher's legitimate educational purposes, including potentially sensitive work content.
assumptions: Assumes the teacher's role requires viewing all student submissions.

title: Teacher may disclose student data to unauthorized parties
description: The teacher may share the received student submissions with unauthorized third parties or beyond their educational role.
assumptions: Assumes the teacher has access to the data and may choose to share it.

title: Teacher may misuse student work content
description: The teacher may use student work content for purposes other than its intended educational purpose, such as commercial use or unauthorized publication.
assumptions: Assumes the teacher has discretion over how to use the received data.

title: Metadata in data flow may link students to teachers
description: The data flow itself may contain metadata (e.g., timestamps, IP addresses, session information) that could be used to link students to specific teachers or correlate data across multiple flows.
assumptions: Assumes the data flow may contain technical metadata beyond the described content.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if metadata is included in the flow; depends on implementation details.

title: Excessive Data Collection at Source
description: Teacher may share more personal data than necessary (e.g., full student name, contact information) when only student ID and grade information are required for the assignment submission.
assumptions: Teacher has discretion over what data to include in the submission

title: Unintended Data Disclosure at Source
description: Teacher may unintentionally include sensitive information in feedback (e.g., personal details about student's family, health information) that should not be shared.
assumptions: Teacher may not be fully aware of all data they are including in feedback

title: Unauthorized Disclosure at Source
description: Teacher may disclose sensitive student information without proper authorization or legal basis, potentially violating privacy policies.
assumptions: Teacher has access to sensitive student data beyond what is needed for grading

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Data in transit between Teacher and Grades Portal Web App could be intercepted or monitored by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be fully encrypted or may traverse unsecured networks

title: Data Leakage During Transmission
description: Data could be leaked or exposed during transmission due to network vulnerabilities or misconfiguration.
assumptions: Network infrastructure may have security gaps

title: Excessive Data Retention at Destination
description: Grades Portal Web App may retain more student data than necessary for the intended purpose (e.g., keeping historical data indefinitely, storing unnecessary metadata).
assumptions: System may have default retention policies that exceed minimum requirements

title: Unauthorized Data Disclosure at Destination
description: Grades Portal Web App may disclose student data to unauthorized parties (e.g., third-party vendors, unauthorized administrators) without proper consent.
assumptions: System may have inadequate access controls or data sharing agreements

title: Unintended Data Processing at Destination
description: Grades Portal Web App may process student data in unintended ways (e.g., using data for purposes other than grading, such as marketing or profiling).
assumptions: System may have multiple data processing purposes not clearly defined or communicated

title: Unintended disclosure of student request data
description: Student's request for grades and feedback could be intercepted or misused by third parties during the sharing process.
assumptions: Assumes the student is requesting their own grades and feedback through the portal.

title: Unintended disclosure of data in transit
description: Data flowing from student to grades portal could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission.
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted over a network connection.

title: Unintended disclosure of grades data
description: Grades portal web app could disclose student grades and feedback to unauthorized parties upon receipt.
assumptions: Assumes the system has appropriate access controls in place.

title: Data minimization violation
description: Grades portal web app may store more student data than necessary for the purpose of providing grades and feedback.
assumptions: Assumes the system collects and stores additional data beyond what is needed for grade retrieval.

title: Data destruction failure
description: Grades portal web app may fail to properly destroy student data when it is no longer needed.
assumptions: Assumes the system has data retention policies in place.

title: Inaccurate or outdated grades displayed
description: The portal may display grades that are outdated, incorrect, or not yet finalized, leading to confusion for the student about their academic standing.
assumptions: Assumes grades are stored in the system and displayed to the student

title: Excessive data disclosure
description: The portal may display more data than necessary for the student to view their grades, potentially including unnecessary metadata or related information.
assumptions: Assumes the portal displays all available grade-related information

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Grades and teacher feedback data transmitted from the portal to the student could potentially be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit.
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted over a network

title: Data corruption during transmission
description: Data transmitted from the portal to the student could be corrupted or altered during transit, resulting in inaccurate information being displayed.
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted over a network

title: Student misinterprets grades
description: The student may misinterpret or misunderstand the grades and teacher feedback displayed, leading to incorrect conclusions about their academic performance.
assumptions: Assumes the student has the ability to read and interpret the displayed information

title: Student inadvertently shares grades
description: The student may inadvertently share their grades or teacher feedback with unauthorized parties through social media or other channels.
assumptions: Assumes the student has access to external communication channels

title: Inappropriate Information Sharing
description: Portal may share more information than necessary for the parent to know about their child's academic progress, potentially including sensitive feedback or submission details that could be inappropriate for a parent to access.
assumptions: Parent has legitimate interest in child's grades, but portal may include excessive or sensitive information

title: Insufficient Notification
description: Parent may not be adequately notified about what specific data is being shared, how it will be used, or with whom it may be shared.
assumptions: Portal may not have clear privacy notices or consent mechanisms for data sharing

title: Unintended Data Disclosure
description: Portal may inadvertently disclose data to unauthorized parties or in unintended contexts, such as through system errors or misconfigured access controls.
assumptions: Portal has access controls but may have configuration errors or vulnerabilities

title: Data Flow Deduction
description: Meta-data about the data flow (e.g., timing, frequency, volume) could be used to link or identify the parent-child relationship or infer sensitive information about the child's academic performance.
assumptions: Data flow metadata may be observable by third parties

title: Parental Deduction of Sensitive Information
description: Parent may deduce sensitive information about the child from the grades, feedback, and submission history, such as learning disabilities, behavioral issues, or family circumstances.
assumptions: Parent may interpret grades and feedback in ways that reveal sensitive personal information

title: Unintended Data Sharing by Parent
description: Parent may inadvertently or intentionally share the child's academic data with unauthorized third parties, such as other parents, schools, or employers.
assumptions: Parent may not be aware of or may disregard privacy policies regarding data sharing

title: Unlawful or Unjustified Data Collection
description: School Administrator may collect and share personal information (names, emails, relationships) without proper legal basis or justification, potentially violating data protection laws.

title: Inaccurate or Incomplete Information
description: Administrator may input inaccurate, outdated, or incomplete personal information about students and parents, leading to incorrect records and potential harm.

title: Excessive Data Collection
description: Administrator may collect more personal data than necessary for the intended purpose, violating data minimization principles.

title: Data Integrity During Transmission
description: Personal data in transit between administrator and web app may be intercepted, modified, or corrupted by malicious actors or network vulnerabilities.

title: Unlawful Data Processing
description: Grades Portal Web App may process personal data without proper legal basis or adequate safeguards, potentially violating privacy laws.

title: Inadequate Information Security
description: Personal information stored in the web app may not be adequately protected against unauthorized access, leading to data breaches.

title: Excessive Data Retention
description: Web app may retain more personal data than necessary for the intended purpose, increasing privacy risks.

title: Unintended Data Consequences
description: Processing and storing of parent-child relationship data may have unintended consequences, such as enabling profiling or tracking of individuals.

title: Inaccurate parent-child relationship links
description: The grading service may write inaccurate parent-child relationship links to the account directory, leading to incorrect account hierarchies and potentially affecting account access or administrative functions.
assumptions: The grading service does not have proper validation for parent-child relationships before writing them to the directory.

title: Excessive data sharing
description: The grading service may share more account data than necessary for the assignment and grading process, including unnecessary parent-child relationship links that could be used for profiling or tracking.
assumptions: The grading service does not minimize data collection to only what is necessary for the grading function.

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Account records and parent-child relationship links may be intercepted during transmission from the grading service to the account directory, exposing sensitive account information to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Data is transmitted without proper encryption or over insecure channels.

title: Inaccurate account records due to improper validation
description: The account directory may not properly validate the account records and parent-child relationship links being written by the grading service, leading to corrupted or inconsistent data that could affect account management.
assumptions: The account directory does not implement proper data validation checks before accepting writes.

title: Account directory unavailability
description: The account directory may become unavailable, preventing the grading service from writing account records and parent-child relationship links, potentially disrupting grading operations.
assumptions: The account directory may experience technical failures, maintenance, or be taken offline.

title: Lack of audit trail for data modifications
description: The grading service may not maintain proper audit trails for changes made to account records, making it difficult to track who made changes and when, which could affect accountability and dispute resolution.
assumptions: The grading service does not implement proper logging mechanisms for data modifications.

title: Data interception during transit
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory are transmitted in transit to the cloud hosting provider. Data could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission, leading to unauthorized access to sensitive student information.
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted over network without guaranteed encryption

title: Metadata leakage during data flow
description: Metadata about the parties being used to link or identify them could be extracted from the data flow, potentially allowing correlation of data with specific students or institutions.
assumptions: Assumes metadata can be extracted from network traffic

title: Unauthorized access to stored data
description: The cloud hosting provider could potentially access the stored grade records, assignments, and account directory without proper authorization, leading to unauthorized disclosure of sensitive student information.
assumptions: Assumes the cloud provider has appropriate security controls

title: Data misuse by third-party provider
description: The cloud hosting provider could potentially use the stored data for purposes other than the intended backup and hosting, such as data profiling or selling to third parties.
assumptions: Assumes the cloud provider has appropriate data usage policies

title: Insecure data storage at destination
description: The cloud hosting provider could store the grade records, assignments, and account directory in an insecure manner, making them vulnerable to unauthorized access or data breaches.
assumptions: Assumes the cloud provider has appropriate security measures

title: Over-sharing of sensitive data
description: The Assignment & Grading Service may be sharing more data than necessary for the backup and hosting purpose, including full grade records and account directory information that could be sensitive.
assumptions: Assumes the data sharing is intentional and necessary

title: Excessive Data Sharing at Source
description: The Grade Records Database may share more data than necessary for the Assignment & Grading Service to build student, parent, and teacher views, potentially exposing sensitive information.
assumptions: Assumes the database contains sensitive student, parent, and teacher information.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain about exact LINDDUN Pro tree node ID; using I.1.1 as a reasonable approximation for information disclosure at source.

title: Data in Transit Information Disclosure
description: Metadata about the parties (students, parents, teachers) in the data flow could be used to link or identify them during transmission.
assumptions: Assumes data flows contain identifiable information about multiple parties.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain about exact LINDDUN Pro tree node ID; using I.1.1 as a reasonable approximation for information disclosure during data flow.

title: Unauthorized Data Disclosure at Destination
description: The Assignment & Grading Service may disclose data to unauthorized parties when building views for students, parents, and teachers.
assumptions: Assumes the service has access to multiple stakeholder views.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain about exact LINDDUN Pro tree node ID; using I.1.1 as a reasonable approximation for information disclosure at destination.

title: Unintended Privacy Consequences from View Building
description: Building views for students, parents, and teachers may have unintended privacy implications, such as revealing information about one party to another without consent.
assumptions: Assumes views may reveal information about multiple parties.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain about exact LINDDUN Pro tree node ID; using U.1.1 as a reasonable approximation for unintended consequences.
